_meta.indication: Treatment of bacterial conjunctivitis caused by susceptible isolates of designated bacteria

pivotal_trials.phase: Adequate and well-controlled (pivotal) superiority efficacy trial vs vehicle supporting approval
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-masked, parallel, vehicle-controlled trial
pivotal_trials.population: Patients at least one year of age with a clinical diagnosis of acute bilateral bacterial conjunctivitis (purulent discharge and redness)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical resolution and eradication of baseline bacterial infection (primary endpoints at Visit 3)
pivotal_trials.n: Culture-positive (mITT) N=60 besifloxacin vs N=56 vehicle
pivotal_trials.result: Modified ITT (culture-positive) clinical resolution at Visit 3 (Day 8): 37/60 (62%) besifloxacin vs 20/56 (36%) vehicle (95% CI 0.0838, 0.4353)

pivotal_trials.phase: Adequate and well-controlled (pivotal) superiority efficacy trial vs vehicle supporting approval
pivotal_trials.population: Patients at least 1 year of age with a clinical diagnosis of acute bacterial conjunctivitis (purulent discharge and redness)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical resolution and microbial eradication of baseline bacterial infection
pivotal_trials.n: Culture-positive (mITT) N=198 besifloxacin vs N=191 vehicle
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical resolution 45% (90/198) besifloxacin vs 33% (63/191) vehicle (difference 12%, 95% CI 3%-22%); microbial eradication 91% (181/198) vs 60% (114/191) (difference 31%, 95% CI 23%-40%)

pivotal_trials.phase: Adequate and well-controlled (pivotal) equivalence efficacy trial vs moxifloxacin supporting approval
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-masked, parallel, active-controlled trial comparing besifloxacin 0.6% to moxifloxacin HCl 0.5%
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with acute bacterial conjunctivitis; same inclusion and exclusion criteria as Study 433 (at least 1 year of age, purulent discharge and redness)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical resolution and eradication of baseline bacterial infection; same primary endpoints as Study 433
pivotal_trials.n: Culture-positive (mITT) N=251 besifloxacin vs N=274 moxifloxacin
pivotal_trials.result: Modified ITT (culture-positive) clinical resolution at Visit 3 (Day 8): 223/251 (89%) besifloxacin vs 232/274 (85%) moxifloxacin (95% CI -1.66%, 10.01%), demonstrating equivalence to moxifloxacin

key_safety: Most common ocular adverse reaction was conjunctival redness (~2%); other reactions (~1-2%) included blurred vision, eye pain, eye irritation, eye pruritus and headache
target_moa: 8-chloro fluoroquinolone antibacterial; inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV (enzymes essential for bacterial DNA replication, transcription, repair and partitioning)

advisory_committee.vote: Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drug Advisory Committee reviewed the NDA on December 5, 2008 and recommended approval

description.text: Added four pathogens (Aerococcus viridans, Moraxella catarrhalis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus warneri) to the microbiology/susceptibility labeling

summary.text: Standard-review NDA (505(b)) for a new molecular entity ophthalmic fluoroquinolone; reviewed by the Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drug Advisory Committee on December 5, 2008 which recommended approval; approved May 2009 with a required 505(o) post-marketing safety clinical trial for 7-day dosing

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated May 30, 2008, received June 2, 2008, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Besivance (besifloxacin ophthalmic suspension) 0.6%.
As the product was a new molecular entity an inspection of the Sponsor was also conducted.
On December 5, 2008 the Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drug Advisory Committee reviewed NDA 22-308. The Advisory recommended approval of besifloxacin hydrochloride ophthalmic suspension, 0.6%.

- A randomized, parallel arm, vehicle-controlled, clinical trial to evaluate the safety of Besivance (besifloxacin ophthalmic suspension) 0.6% when administered three times a day, four to twelve hours apart for 7 days. The clinical trial must enroll at least 300 patients with signs and symptoms of bacterial conjunctivitis (ocular redness and discharge). You may wish to randomize patients in a 2:1 ratio, Besivance: control, for the objective of collecting safety data from the trial. Subjects should also be followed for clinical outcomes as this information can be important in the assessment of the safety data from the trial. Microbial cultures are required at baseline.

requirement.text: A randomized, parallel-arm, vehicle-controlled clinical trial (at least 300 patients with bacterial conjunctivitis) to evaluate safety of Besivance administered three times a day for 7 days
